title: Service signal card: build a data-driven Canvas

blocks.content: Build a service signal card with a numeric value, a threshold-driven background, and an aligned label. This standalone lab uses synthetic TestData; its colors do not assess production service health.
Open **Dashboards** as the starting point for this lab.
Open **Dashboards** to begin.
blocks.tooltip: Open Dashboards to begin with a saved workspace.

blocks.content: You have opened the workspace where you will create your practice dashboard.
Prepare a TestData source if your organization does not already have one.

blocks.tooltip: Open the shared Add data source page.
blocks.content: Open **Add data source**.

blocks.tooltip: Find TestData; no external service or credentials are needed.
blocks.content: Search for **TestData**.

blocks.tooltip: Create the TestData source.
blocks.content: Click **TestData** to create the data source.
TestData supplies synthetic values without an external service or credentials.

whenTrue.prompt: Select your TestData source; its name may differ in your organization.

whenFalse.content: Complete TestData setup before choosing the practice source; an administrator can create it if needed.

blocks.content: Create a new dashboard, select your practice source, and choose Canvas.
Create a fresh dashboard for this lab.
blocks.tooltip: Create a fresh dashboard for this lab.

blocks.content: Open **Add** to show the controls for creating a panel.
blocks.tooltip: Show the controls for adding dashboard elements.

blocks.content: Click **Panel** to add a panel.
blocks.tooltip: Add a panel for your synthetic signals.

blocks.content: Click **Edit visualization** to open the panel editor.
blocks.tooltip: Open the visualization editor.

blocks.content: In the data source picker, select {{practiceSource}}.
blocks.tooltip: Query the existing source chosen for this lab.

blocks.content: Choose the Canvas visualization.

steps.tooltip: Open the visualization chooser.
Select Canvas.

blocks.content: In **Panel options**, set **Title** to `Service signal card`.
blocks.tooltip: Give the panel a recognizable name.

blocks.content: Canvas gives you a workspace where individual elements can display query fields.
Generate one random signal bounded between 0 and 100.
In query **A**, set **Min** to `0`.
blocks.tooltip: Keep the synthetic values at or above zero.

blocks.content: In query **A**, set **Max** to `100`.
blocks.tooltip: Cap the synthetic values at 100.

blocks.content: In query **A**, set **Start value** to `50`.
blocks.tooltip: Start the random walk halfway through the range.

blocks.content: Run the query to see your practice data.
blocks.tooltip: Run the query to see your practice data.

blocks.content: A bounded random walk makes it easier to interpret this practice card.
Name the metric element in the layer tree, then bind it to a query field: the name helps you find the element, while the binding supplies its displayed number.

blocks.title: Bind a value to the canvas

blocks.content: In **Canvas**, turn off **Experimental element types** to use the standard elements.
blocks.tooltip: Keep the practice layout on standard element types.

blocks.content: In **Layer**, select **Element 1** in **Elements**.
blocks.tooltip: Select the starting metric element from the layer tree.

blocks.content: Name the metric layer Signal value.

steps.description: Give the metric element a useful layer name.
steps.tooltip: Make this layer easier to identify when editing the layout.
Name this element Signal value.

blocks.content: In **Metric value**, set **Text** to **A-series** to display its latest non-null sample.
blocks.tooltip: Read the number from the query field instead of entering fixed text.

blocks.content: In **Standard options**, set **Decimals** to `1`.
blocks.tooltip: Show enough precision for this practice signal without crowding the card.

blocks.content: In **Metric value**, set **Text size** to `36` to make the number prominent.
blocks.tooltip: Make the signal value prominent.

blocks.content: The layer name identifies the element, while its field binding supplies the displayed value.
Make the background respond to the signal: a fixed color stays unchanged, while a field binding uses that field’s value and thresholds to choose its color.
In **Thresholds**, set the existing threshold to `70`; this colors values at or above 70 differently without creating an alert.
blocks.tooltip: Use this boundary to demonstrate a color change without creating an alert.

blocks.content: In **Background**, set **Color** to **A-series** so the field’s threshold color fills this element.
blocks.tooltip: Use the same field for the value and its threshold-driven color.

blocks.content: The number shows the latest non-null sample. Its background follows field thresholds, not a fixed paint color.
blocks.tooltip: The number shows the latest non-null sample. Its background follows field thresholds, not a fixed paint color.

blocks.content: Field thresholds drive the background color; the threshold does not create an alert.

blocks.question: What makes the card background respond to the signal?

choices.text: Binding the background to A-series and using its thresholds.
Giving the metric layer a descriptive name.
Setting a fixed background paint color.

blocks.content: Set the value card dimensions and position numerically.
In **Layout** → **Quick placement**, set **width** to `280` and **height** to `100` to size the value card.

steps.tooltip: Give the value card a comfortable width.
Make the value card tall enough for the large number.

blocks.content: In **Layout** → **Quick placement**, set **top** to `90` and **left** to `40` to leave room for a label above the card.

steps.tooltip: Leave room above the value for a label.
Place the value card with a consistent left margin.

blocks.content: Explicit dimensions and offsets make the layout repeatable.
Add a centered service label and align it above the value card.

blocks.title: Add a label that explains the value

blocks.content: Add a text element.

steps.tooltip: Open the element picker.
Add a Text element.

blocks.content: Name the text layer Service label.

steps.tooltip: Make this layer easier to identify when editing the layout.

steps.description: Use Service label in the layer tree.
steps.tooltip: Use Service label in the layer tree.

blocks.content: In **Text**, set **Text** to `Checkout - practice` to give the number context.
blocks.tooltip: Give the changing number a clear service context.

blocks.content: In **Text**, set **Text size** to `24`.
blocks.tooltip: Make the label readable.

blocks.content: In **Text**, set **Align text** to **Center**.
blocks.tooltip: Align the label centrally above the numeric value.

blocks.content: In **Layout** → **Quick placement**, set **width** to `280` and **height** to `50` to match the card’s width.

steps.tooltip: Match the label width to the value card.
Give the label a compact height.

blocks.content: In **Layout** → **Quick placement**, set **top** to `30` and **left** to `40` to align the label above the card.

steps.tooltip: Place the label above the value card.
Align the label with the card.

blocks.content: Separate text and metric elements let you combine context with a changing value.
Disable inline editing and inspect the completed practice card.
In **Canvas**, turn off **Inline editing** to prevent dashboard clicks from moving elements.
blocks.tooltip: Keep dashboard interactions from accidentally moving the finished layout.

blocks.content: Inspect the label and data-bound card; this is a demonstration, not a production health assessment.
blocks.tooltip: Inspect the label and data-bound card; this is a demonstration, not a production health assessment.

blocks.content: Turning off inline editing protects the layout from accidental movement.

blocks.question: What does disabling inline editing do?

choices.text: Prevents dashboard clicks from moving Canvas elements.
Stops the query from refreshing its values.

blocks.content: Save the dashboard and check that the label and numeric value remain visible.
Click **Back** to return to the dashboard.
blocks.tooltip: Return to the dashboard.

blocks.content: Save this dashboard as Canvas lab - Service signal card.

steps.description: Click **Save** to open the save drawer.
steps.tooltip: Open the save drawer.
Give this practice dashboard a recognizable name for later retrieval.
Save the dashboard.

blocks.content: Inspect the saved Canvas lab - Service signal card dashboard: Checkout - practice should sit above a large numeric value, the background should follow the illustrative threshold at 70, and inline editing should be off.
blocks.tooltip: Inspect the saved dashboard and check the finished configuration.

blocks.content: Your saved dashboard preserves the labelled card and its data-driven configuration.
Import a separate five-service example with manually drawn connections to see how these techniques scale into a systems map; your service signal card remains saved.

blocks.title: This is what you can build

blocks.content: Build a five-service systems map. This block inserts a complete dashboard definition, connects your TestData source, and saves Canvas lab - Checkout systems map.

steps.tooltip: Open dashboard import to create a separate example map.

blocks.content: Follow Gateway → Checkout, then the arrows to Payments, Inventory, and Database. Inventory is red at 86%, Database is orange at 61%, and the remaining services are green. Each number and background binds to its own query field. These are fixed synthetic utilization samples; the connections are drawn explicitly, not discovered automatically.
blocks.tooltip: Inspect the connected services and find the illustrative utilization hotspot.

blocks.content: Your card and connected map combine positioned elements, field bindings, thresholds, and directional connections that you can adapt to your own system.
